about.size: Up to about 48 inches and 50 lb; Florida state record 45 lb 12 oz (FWC).
about.diet: Primarily fishes and large crustaceans. FWC lists live pinfish, small mullet, shrimp and sardines among effective baits; diet studies document fishes and crustaceans.
about.behavior: Inshore coastal fish using mangrove shorelines, seagrass beds, beaches, channels, river mouths and other structure. Snook orient into moving water and ambush prey carried by the current. Juveniles use sheltered mangrove-lined swamps, bayous, rivers and creeks; adults use broad estuarine habitat and move between upper-estuary overwintering areas and higher-salinity spawning sites.
about.spawning: Florida spawning generally runs April/May through September/October. Major inlets and coastal river mouths are documented spawning locations. Exact annual timing varies with climate and temperature.
about.timing_note: Angler lore: patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies. Numbers are judgment calls to be calibrated against trip logs.

factor_diagnostics.value_notes: FWC and lab studies support a lower cold-stress boundary around 14–16 °C, while a 2025 Everglades analysis found a positive relationship between common snook relative abundance and temperature. A 2025 juvenile thermal-tolerance study shows body size and salinity affect cold tolerance. These sources support temperature relevance but do not validate a universal adult optimum or the full 15.6–35 °C / 24–32 °C ideal band.
